authored.note: Explanations are written for learners. Facts are checked word for word against the cited files. The events shown in Practice are the committed specimen packs, unedited.

summary.text: The first tool call here is legitimate and succeeds. The question is what happens next: can the text that call returned give the agent permission to call a different tool? Three recorded runs show a normal result, a malicious result let through by an intentionally weak profile, and the same malicious result refused by the defended profile.
facts: an authorized tool is not an authoritative result.

glance.label: The legitimate operation
glance.text: The first hop is a granted lookup_policy call against the granted lending-basics resource. The handler runs and returns data.

glance.label: What the attacker controls
glance.text: The content of the tool's result. The attacker does not touch the request; the malicious bytes come back inside a legitimate response.
facts: malicious tool-result content used as result-derived authority

glance.label: The trust boundary
glance.text: Between the tool result and whatever the agent decides to do next. The result sits on the data side of that line.

glance.label: The authorization rule
glance.text: Results can inform what the agent thinks. They never create permission; the follow-on tool still needs its own grant.
facts: Tool results may influence reasoning. Tool results do not create authority.

glance.label: What this evidence is, and is not
glance.text: In the attack run the follow-on request is supplied by the lab as an overlay, not chosen by a model. A model obeying injected text is not what this recording shows.
facts: Explain why ATTACK follow-on is labeled ALLOW (overlay, not server grant).
Explain why this lab is not prompt-injection resistance.

known.text: The recorded content preview is capped at 200 characters, so a long request can be cut off mid-word. The pack shows exactly what was recorded.
The lab records no indexed list of the tools the server granted. Do not infer one.
facts: no indexed `allowed_tools` — SERVER AUTHORITY EVIDENCE — LIMITED
